lesson.title: Saying it in your own words
lesson.skill: Explain a two-step move in your own words, without looking at the lesson.
lesson.missionLink: You can solve the problems and still freeze if someone asks you why the order matters. Two prompts to practise saying it out loud.

primarySource.why: It states the reason for the order in one sentence, which is what the prompts ask you to reproduce.

content.text: Write these from memory. Nobody sees what you type until you have finished the lesson, so there is nothing to look up and nothing to lose by getting it wrong.

blocks.prompt: In your own words, why do you undo addition before you undo multiplication?

content.text: One more, because the second one is the one that catches people out.

blocks.prompt: In your own words, what makes an equation checkable?

content.text: Read them back to yourself afterwards. The sentence you can say without hesitating is the one you actually have.
